Chris — appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a compact options workbook (novamorph-reserve-options.xlsx) and below is a single-page summary to share with procurement/finance. High-level rationale and three options tailored to your forecast: pilot -> prod -> scale.

Option A — Foundational (conservative)
- Reserved: 8 H100 GPUs (min floor)
- Burst: up to 24 via shared burst pool (best-effort, short-lived)
- Ramp: pilot (July) use 8 reserved; prod (Sept) add 8-16 burst-enabled; Q4 remain at 8 reserved, use burst for spikes
- Tradeoffs: lowest monthly commitment; higher tail latency on sustained spikes

Option B — Production Baseline (recommended for 100k tokens/day steady)
- Reserved: 24 H100 GPUs (min floor)
- Burst: additional 40 GPUs available from burst pool (autoscaled, billed only when used)
- Ramp: July pilot 8 reserved + 8 burst; Sept activate 24 reserved; Oct–Dec scale bursts to handle 3x steady peaks
- Tradeoffs: predictable throughput, consistent latency, lower per-token cost vs A

Option C — Scale-Ready (for aggressive growth)
- Reserved: 64 mixed GPUs (32 H100 reserved + 32 warm H100/A100 pool)
- Burst: dedicated warm lane with capacity pre-warmed (recommended for sustained high concurrency)
- Ramp: staged 32 reserved in Sept, activate remaining 32 in Nov once throughput triggers met
- Tradeoffs: higher commitment, best latency and warm-cache hit rates

Operational suggestions across options:
- Warm-start: pre-load model KV cache to cover top 10% of traffic patterns before major launches (adds ~10–18% GPU memory overhead during warm window).
- Canary: 5% traffic to canary model for 48–72 hours; automated rollback if latency/P65 token cost deviates >15% or error rate increases.
- Caching + routing: enable prefix caching for common prompts and route short-latency requests to smaller quantized variants to save cost.

Next steps: Marissa can follow up with a deployment diagram and timeline; Karthik will validate minimum GPU floor for your expected mix of chat vs batch. If this looks good, we'll prepare an SOW and a slot in our activation calendar (we have a warm-start window the week of Aug 16).

Attachments: novamorph-reserve-options.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales – Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi Chris / Laura — addressing your asks and putting numbers behind Option B (the recommended baseline). Summary below and I've dropped the activation timeline PNG in the attachments for calendar planning.

SLA + credits
- Reserved lane SLA: 99.95% monthly availability for reserved GPUs. Credits: prorated service credit tiers starting at 5% for >0.5% monthly downtime, escalating for longer outages; for outages > 1 hour we offer a defined remediation + credit path in the SOW.

Burst billing (example pricing, GPU-hour basis)
- Burst rate (H100 hot lane): $6.50 per GPU-hour
- Reserved amortized (monthly): shown in spreadsheet; example estimate below for 24 reserved + 20 burst at 50% avg burst utilization:
  - Reserved (24): fixed monthly commit => baseline cost X (see workbook)
  - Burst (20 * 50% * hours in month -> GPU-hours): ~7200 GPU-hours -> $46,800 at $6.50/hr
  - We will include a burn table in the spreadsheet for finance to model several utilization points.

Compatibility and mixed pool notes
- H100/A100 mixed pool: supported for stateless inference but we recommend pinning large, latency-sensitive models to H100s and using A100s for less latency-sensitive batch work. For your quantized pipeline (70% FP16 / 30% INT8) we recommend forcing INT8 inference to A100 warm lanes to avoid precision regressions during hot swaps; our runtime transparently routes by model tag.

Commit structure suggestion
- 12-month commit: 1 trial month at 40% discount, then steady monthly commitment. Q4 expansion clause: unilateral option to add +30% reserved capacity with 60-day notice; pricing floor holds.

Action items
- Kimberly: well draft SOW + activation calendar (include warm-start week of Aug 16)
- Karthik: confirm minimum floor readiness for 24 reserved with current model memory profile
- Chris / Laura: confirm preferred option (A / B / C) and any procurement constraints by EOD next Wednesday so we can lock dates.
